 Meredith Jacobs Thu, November 19, 2026 at 1:25 PM UTC 2 min read Add Yahoo as a preferred source to see more of our stories on Google. Scott Speedman — 'R.J. Decker' - Disney/Dana Hawley One of the broadcast shows whose future is very much up in the air is  R.J. Decker . It received only a seven-episode order for Season 2 (the finale has already aired) and it was the last series renewed by ABC in May. Now there seems to be even more reason to wonder about a potential Season 3: a new role for lead Scott Speedman .
 Speedman will be guest starring in  Landman Season 3, with character details not yet revealed. That also means we don't know how big a role he'll have in the upcoming season, and whether it could extend long enough to affect potential production on  R.J. Decker . But there's not necessarily reason to be worried.
 Speedman has had no trouble leading  R.J. Decker and continuing to recur on  Grey's Anatomy , and Landman is already in production on Season 3 in Texas, according to Deadline . Chances are there will be no overlap for production on the Taylor Sheridan series and a potential Season 3 of  R.J. Decker since ABC likely won't be making a decision on the latter until close to or in May and it could be a fall or midseason series for the 2027-2028 season, should it return. Therefore, this new gig shouldn't affect his series regular one at all. But we still have to wait to see if ABC wants more  R.J. 
 Bevin Bru and Scott Speedman — 'R.J. Decker' Season 2 Disney/Dana Hawley
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement R.J. Decker 's second season did leave off on a major cliffhanger. Mel ( Bevin Bru ) discovered that her friend and fellow officer was actually killed by his wife, Jessica, years ago, meaning an innocent man was sent to prison. As the finale ended, Jessica called Mel and let her know she was watching — and approaching — her wife ( Adelaide Clemens ) and daughter.

 "We have to swing for the fences," showrunner Rob Doherty told TV Insider of ending the season that way. "I mean, it is true that we are through two whole seasons, but it's also true that those two seasons add up to exactly 16 episodes. We want more. We want to plan for success. We want to give a reason for everyone to come back to the show if and when the time comes. So we feel confident in that we have great partners at ABC and at 20th. We feel like they've done a great job of promoting the show. So yeah, we want to tee up more. We want to be ready for more. We want to be ready for a third season."
